catalog_quote: [Abstract p.1] A Foot in Paite is categorized as syllabic – iamb and feet construction is both binary as well as unbounded. Paite is a Quantity – Insensitive language and the metrical rhythmic pattern is controlled by the tone – alternation pattern. [4.6, p.76] Evidence that the basic foot – inventory of Paite is an iambic - system comes from the following tone – alternations triggered by vowel shortenings found in disyllables (from 1.3 b) and tri – syllables in (b) ... [p.78] The foot – parsing of (a) and (b) above is blind to the notion quantity, that is, the moras are the tone – bearing units and at each level, the parsing units which is equivalent to tones are delinked to avoid clashes and project only a fully – toned syllable at the right – margin. The foot parsing of (b) is unbounded while that of (a) is binary. [p.81, end-note 3] The usage of moras is to show a tone – bearing units but not weight – units. Paite is a weight – insensitive language. [ch.3 sec. 3.7, p.43] The tonemes of Paite is composed of minimal contrasting pairs known as minimal triplets and other tonemes conditioned by the presence of voiceless stop coda /p, t, k/ and glottal stop coda /ʔ/ to give rise to a total of five (5) tonemes in Paite.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Paite is a tone language (5 tonemes) with no lexical stress contrast; word-level prominence is analysed as a quantity-insensitive syllabic iamb: in compounds/polysyllables the non-final syllables shorten and lose their tone while the final (rightmost) syllable keeps full tone and length, i.e. right-edge (final-syllable) prominence; feet may be binary or unbounded.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; non-head syllables are simply de-toned/shortened.
new_statements.exceptions: Nominalisation with the toned suffix -na: yields left/trochaic prominence on the stem (luak-na:, te:t-na:), attributed to clash avoidance; H-tone spread in reduplicative adverbs gives right-edge prominence. Function words not treated.
new_statements.domain_note: Prosodic word (stem + affixes, compounds) elicited as words and compounds read in isolation by four JNU-student speakers; prominence is diagnosed from tone/vowel-length alternation (Praat F0), not from stress phonetics. Theory-laden (Hayes/Kager metrical terms); the author never states a plain 'stress falls on X' rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Nianglianmoi 2016 describes Paite of Manipur (speakers recorded at JNU; Lamzang treated as standard, Lamka town koine noted); Singh 1985 describes the Lamjang (Lamzang) dialect of Tuithapi village near Churachandpur; Grierson 1904's 'Paite' is the Dapzal variety of the Lushai Hills. All fall under pait1244. Henderson 1965 (list of works to obtain) describes Tedim/Tiddim Chin of Myanmar, a separate glottocode (tedi1235) though authors treat Paite and Tedim as one dialect cluster.

sources.locator: Abstract p.[1]; ch.4 sec. 4.6 p.76 and p.78 (pp.12,14 of); end-note 3 p.81
sources.note: Ch.4 'Prosodic Word': Paite feet are quantity-insensitive syllabic iambs; in di-/trisyllabic words non-final syllables shorten/lose tone and only the rightmost syllable projects full tone (right-margin prominence); nominaliser -na gives trochaic (stem) prominence; 'Paite is a weight-insensitive language'; rhythm is controlled by tone alternation. No lexical stress contrast is posited; five tonemes (M, H, L, LH, HL).
